stem: Which approach best supports an individual nurse's ongoing professional development?

options.A: Identify individualized learning and role-development needs and plan relevant development activities.
options.B: Use identical development goals for every nurse regardless of role, competence, or career stage.
options.C: Limit professional development to disciplinary remediation after performance problems occur.
options.D: Avoid planned development activities because professional growth should occur without structured support.

rationale: Nursing professional development is intended to facilitate ongoing learning, role competence, and professional growth. Current NPD standards emphasize education and role development as core responsibilities and account for the learner as an input to professional-development planning. A is correct because development should address the nurse's identified learning and role needs rather than use a one-size-fits-all or discipline-only model.
educational_objective: Recognize individualized, planned learning and role development as core elements of nursing professional development.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), StatPearls
source_version_date: Last Update September 20, 2022; current NPD standards summary checked 2026-08-17
source_locator: Definition/Introduction — NPD definition; systems practice model inputs and key responsibilities including education and role development
source_claim_supported: Nursing professional development facilitates ongoing learning, role competence, and growth; education and role development are core NPD responsibilities and the learner is part of the planning model.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — staff education, professional development, and resource management

source_original.stem: A nurse works with their manager to create an individualized professional development plan. This plan typically includes:

options.A: Set individualized development goals with specific actions and a realistic review timeline
options.B: Use identical development goals for every nurse regardless of experience or career interest
options.C: Limit professional development plans to disciplinary deficiencies rather than career growth
options.D: Avoid specific goals because professional development should occur without formal planning

source_original.rationale: An individualized professional development plan typically includes specific, personalized goals related to skill development, further education, certification, or career advancement, along with a realistic plan and timeline for achieving them, supporting the nurse's ongoing professional growth aligned with their interests and organizational needs.
source_original.source_detail: Professional development planning includes individualized learning/career goals and planned activities; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: The original ANA continuing-education page did not directly support the detailed timeline claim. Rebuilt the item around the NPD standards' supported concepts of learner-specific ongoing learning, education, role development, competence, and growth.

audit_findings.source_authority: NCBI summary of 2022 NPD Scope and Standards; NCSBN 2026

audit_findings.claim_audit: Final wording stays within ongoing learning, role competence/growth, education, role development, and learner-specific planning.

distractor_audit.C: Too narrow; NPD is not limited to remediation.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: A uniquely reflects the NPD model.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe development approaches with similar structure.
audit_findings.blueprint: Staff/professional development fits Management of Care.
